alerts.title: Carbamazepine co-administration reduces dolutegravir levels; virologic failure risk
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. The patient is on DTG (TLD) and was started on carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily two weeks ago. Viral load has risen from <50 copies/mL (2025-09-01) to 1,240 copies/mL today, temporally consistent with this interaction. Adherence is reported good, so reduced drug exposure rather than non-adherence is a plausible explanation, although other causes of viraemia were not excluded in the notes.

evidence.recommended_action: Avoid carbamazepine with DTG; use valproic acid instead per guideline. Coordinate with neurology to change anti-epileptic. Repeat viral load in 2-3 months with enhanced adherence support.

alerts.title: Viral load detectable: enhanced adherence support and repeat testing required
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for VL >50 copies/mL on DTG-based ART, enhanced adherence support should be provided, side-effects affecting adherence addressed, and VL repeated in 2-3 months. Today's VL is 1,240 copies/mL. Given the carbamazepine interaction, the current plan to reduce carbamazepine dose alone does not address the underlying DTG exposure problem.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, repeat VL in 2-3 months, and consider genotype testing if VL remains elevated despite interventions.

alerts.title: Plan review: address carbamazepine-DTG interaction, not just carbamazepine dose
alerts.message: The current plan is to reduce carbamazepine dose and repeat the level. Guidelines recommend avoiding the carbamazepine-DTG combination altogether by using valproic acid. The patient already takes valproate, and the carbamazepine toxicity (level 14 mcg/mL, nystagmus, ataxia, tremor) and hyponatraemia (Na 128 mmol/L) also warrant urgent neurology review.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue carbamazepine in favour of valproic acid per guideline, in consultation with neurology. Address sodium 128 mmol/L and reassess neurological toxicity.
